security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown references, catalog entries, and code-fence markers. The anti-bot bypass and blocked-site access entries are confirmed low-risk content issues because they can guide evasion of site controls. No evidence found for prompt injection or hidden data exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Replace bypass language with guidance limited to authorized scraping, site terms, and robots.txt compliance.
Avoid routing users to access blocked sites unless the task states clear authorization and lawful purpose.

content.user_title: Choose the Right Agent or Skill
content.value_statement: Selecting an AI helper can slow work when agent and skill catalogs overlap. This skill maps task intent to the most suitable Claude, Codex, or Claude Code tool.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use a lightweight skill instead of a heavier agent.
Maps common developer tasks to named skills and agents.
Provides quick references for file formats, CLI tools, and domain libraries.
Points users to detailed agent and skill catalogs for deeper selection.
Recommends skill-first routing for common language, framework, and infrastructure work.
limitations: It recommends tools but does not execute agents or skills directly.
Catalog entries may not match every local Codex or Claude Code installation.
It does not verify whether suggested CLI tools or packages are installed.
Scraping recommendations need authorization checks before use.

use_cases.title: Start a Coding Task
use_cases.description: Choose a focused skill before asking an agent to inspect a repository.

use_cases.title: Route Support Questions
use_cases.description: Select a reference skill for quick answers about formats, commands, or frameworks.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Decide when a multi-step investigation needs a subagent instead of a static reference.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to recommend the best skill or agent for this task: [describe task].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing between a skill and an agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to compare skill-first and agent-first approaches for: [describe workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to design a sequence of skills and agents for this project: [project summary].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tool Choice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tool-discovery to review this tool plan, identify overuse of agents, and suggest simpler skill alternatives.

output_examples.input: I need to find files by name and inspect matching code paths.
output_examples.output: Use file-search first for fast discovery. Use Explore only if the search results need broader investigation.

output_examples.input: I need help with React Server Components behavior.
output_examples.output: Use react-ops first because this is framework reference work. Use a general subagent only for repository-specific diagnosis.

output_examples.input: I need to reorganize a large project directory.
output_examples.output: Use project-organizer because the task requires decisions about structure, ownership, and cleanup scope.

best_practices: Start with the narrowest relevant skill before using a subagent.
Use agents for decisions, trade-offs, and multi-step investigations.
Check catalog references when the task spans more than one domain.
anti_patterns: Do not launch a broad agent for a simple lookup task.
Do not recommend more than two or three tools for one request.
Do not use scraping guidance without confirming authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It recommends the best skill, agent, or reference tool for a user task.

faq.question: Does it run other tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides routing guidance and catalog references only.

faq.question: When should I use a skill?
faq.answer: Use a skill for reference material, patterns, commands, and focused domain guidance.

faq.question: When should I use an agent?
faq.answer: Use an agent for complex decisions, planning, optimization, or multi-step investigation.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The catalog is written for Claude and Claude Code style skill and agent routing.

faq.question: Can Codex users benefit from it?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex users can apply the same routing logic to choose focused references before broader automation.
